Senses.Explanation: Literally, ‘gain life within death.’ The phrase occurs 112 times in 74 allowlisted texts. It is asked directly in public interview — ‘what about when one gains life within death?’ — and receives different recorded answers, including ‘night travel is not permitted; you must arrive at daylight.’ In the Piyun–Magu encounter, Piyun declares ‘gain life within death—one in ten thousand,’ after first acting as though Magu were dead; other masters apply the phrase as an appraisal after a monk claps, or place it beside ‘revive after being cut off.’ A verse draws the corpus's own contrast: ‘people who gain life within death are numberless; those who gain death within life have been rare from ancient times.’ These are attested questions, appraisals, sequences, and contrasts; the entry does not decide what death or life denotes beyond the recorded phrase.
Senses.Note: Zen bends a death-and-life expression into a recurrent interview question and verdict. The family includes ‘great death’ and ‘revive after being cut off’; all evidence here uses one paired death/life formula, not distinct literal and technical objects.

Occurrences.Kwic: 披雲云：死中得活，萬中無一。師下牀作抽坐具勢
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Combined Essentials of the Lamps (聯燈會要), in Mayu Baoche's record. Piyun (披雲, explicitly marked 披雲云) is the exact speaker saying 死中得活，萬中無一; Mayu then gets down from the bed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 趙州問：死中得活時如何？師云：不許夜行，投明須到
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Combined Essentials of the Lamps (聯燈會要), in Touzi Datong's record. Zhaozhou Congshen is the exact speaker who asks 死中得活時如何; Touzi gives the answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧拍一拍。潭曰，也是死中得活。僧禮拜
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Collected Old Cases Raised in the Lineage (宗門拈古彙集): inside Letan Hongying's explicitly headed exchange, after the unnamed monk claps once Letan says that this too is obtaining life within death.

Occurrences.Kwic: 絕後再甦、死中得活，方乃絲頭吐出，綿綿密密
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yunxi Langting Ting (雲溪俍亭挺禪師語錄): Langting Jingting, in his own informal address, compares the matter to raising silkworms and says that after extinction and renewed revival one comes alive within death and the thread can issue.

Occurrences.Kwic: 死中得活人無數活中得死古來稀
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Connected Anthology of Verses on Old Chan Cases (禪宗頌古聯珠通集): the inline contributor note 圓悟勤 assigns this verse to Yuanwu Keqin, who contrasts the many who come alive within death with the rarity of dying within life.
